_purpose: The Researcher reads these as fallback themes AND as a live news watchlist. Use sources for ANGLES, TOPICS, and VERIFIED STATS only. NEVER copy article text into captions. Read a source, extract the idea, then write original Techs4Tatas copy. Treat all source text as copyrighted.

researcher_usage.how_to_use: Each week, the Researcher (or Dave, manually) scans 1-3 news_sources for fresh, relevant items: a new stat, a tradeswoman milestone, a seasonal hook, an awareness angle. It extracts the IDEA and feeds it to the Generator as a brief. The Generator writes original copy.
researcher_usage.copyright_rule: Do not reproduce headlines, sentences, or paragraphs from any source. Paraphrase facts; rewrite everything in brand voice. Cite a stat's origin in your own words (e.g. 'per the American Cancer Society') without quoting.
researcher_usage.cadence: Pairs with the weekly review workflow — scan sources when you review the queue (see review-workflow.md).

The double-standard of being underestimated on a jobsite
Strength + femininity as complements, not opposites
Apprentice-to-pro journeys and mentorship between women
Jobsite humor only tradeswomen will get
The 30% donation as proof the brand walks the walk

_data_hooks_note: Each hook carries a 'beat' field (women_in_trades | breast_cancer) so the Researcher can route the right stat to the right content type (trades_stat vs awareness_stat/mission). 'note' starting with VERIFIED is fully cite-ready; RE-VERIFY items are good drafts but Dave should spot-check the live figure before it posts (BLS/industry numbers move yearly). women_in_trades hooks also carry 'stat' (the short numeral/label rendered BIG on the image card) and 'context' (one short line under it) so the Designer can draw the number directly — it never depends on Claude/evergreen text matching the verified figure. A null 'stat' means the hook is caption-only (no clean numeral) and the post falls back to the standard hook-card layout.

data_hooks.claim: Women are roughly 3% of electricians, plumbers, and carpenters on the tools — still rare, still growing.
data_hooks.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (2025 occupational data)
data_hooks.context: of electricians, plumbers & carpenters on the tools are women
data_hooks.note: Use as 'rare and rising' framing. RE-VERIFY before posting — BLS updates yearly.

data_hooks.claim: Women are about 11-12% of the overall construction workforce (much lower for on-site trade roles specifically).
data_hooks.context: of the overall construction workforce is women (most off the tools)
data_hooks.note: Distinguish 'industry' (includes office roles) vs 'on the tools' (low single digits) for an honest hook.

data_hooks.claim: Skilled-trade demand is surging as retirements outpace new entrants.
data_hooks.note: Great hook for 'the trades need more women' angle. No clean numeral — caption-only, falls back to standard hook card.

data_hooks.claim: Women make up only about 3.1% of plumbers and 3.5% of electricians nationally.
data_hooks.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Population Survey occupational data (2025)
data_hooks.note: RE-VERIFY before posting (BLS updates the table yearly). Sharpest 'on the tools' framing — pair with a proud, defiant tone, not a pity-party one.

data_hooks.claim: Only about 8% of registered apprentices nationwide are women.
data_hooks.source: U.S. Dept. of Labor, Apprenticeship USA data
data_hooks.context: of registered trade apprentices nationwide are women
data_hooks.note: RE-VERIFY before posting. Good for an 'apprentice to pro' / mentorship hook.

data_hooks.claim: The U.S. Dept. of Commerce's 'Million Women in Construction' initiative aims to double women's share of the construction workforce from about 5% to 10% within a decade.
data_hooks.context: the federal goal: double women's share of construction workers
data_hooks.note: RE-VERIFY before posting. Frame as 'the industry itself says it needs more of us' — institutional backup for the brand's mission.

data_hooks.claim: Tradeswomen in construction/extraction occupations grew roughly 77% between 2015 and 2024, topping 366,000.
data_hooks.source: Manufacturers Alliance, 'Women in the Trades: Closing the Talent Gap'
data_hooks.context: growth in tradeswomen since 2015 — 366,000+ and counting
data_hooks.note: RE-VERIFY before posting. Best 'rising fast' growth-stat hook — pairs well with a hype/momentum tone.

data_hooks.claim: Roughly 7% of HVACR companies are woman-owned.
data_hooks.source: Women in HVACR / ITI Technical College
data_hooks.note: RE-VERIFY before posting. Use for an 'owning the business, not just the tools' entrepreneurship angle.

data_hooks.claim: Some industry trackers argue the real on-the-tools share of women in skilled trades is closer to 3%, not the often-quoted 5%.
data_hooks.context: is the real on-the-tools number — not the often-quoted 5%
data_hooks.note: RE-VERIFY before posting. Honest-numbers angle — 'don't believe the rounded-up stat, we know how rare we still are.'

data_hooks.claim: Women hold around 11% of all construction-industry jobs once office and support roles are counted — far higher than the on-the-tools trade-specific share.
data_hooks.source: National Center for Women's Equity in Apprenticeship & Employment
data_hooks.context: of all construction-industry jobs are held by women (incl. office roles)
data_hooks.note: RE-VERIFY before posting. Use to draw an honest line between 'industry' and 'on the tools' so the brand never overstates progress.

data_hooks.claim: About 1 in 8 women (~13%) in the US will develop invasive breast cancer in her lifetime.
data_hooks.note: VERIFIED for 2026. Core awareness stat — strong for mission posts + October.

data_hooks.claim: An estimated 321,910 US women will be diagnosed with invasive breast cancer in 2026; about 42,140 will die.
data_hooks.note: VERIFIED for 2026. Use sparingly — heavy stat, best for awareness/October.

data_hooks.claim: On average, a woman in the US is diagnosed with breast cancer every 2 minutes.
data_hooks.note: VERIFIED. Punchy, emotionally resonant — good single-line hook.

data_hooks.claim: When breast cancer is caught early (localized), the 5-year relative survival rate is over 99%.
data_hooks.note: VERIFIED. Pairs the donation with a genuinely useful early-detection reminder. Hopeful tone.

data_hooks.claim: Breast cancer death rates have fallen ~44% since 1989, thanks to early detection and better treatment.
data_hooks.note: VERIFIED. Use to show donations/research actually move the needle — optimistic, mission-aligned.
